note: Metric-bound readiness backlog. Each task names a ds:score v3 metric, so completion is a number that moved rather than a self-report. Companion prose: readiness-backlog.md
method: current values measured at 04b0bfa by `npm run ds:score --json` on 2026-10-08, rubric v4. `current` is the metric's 0-100 SCORE, not its raw count; `raw` carries the underlying figures. v3 and v4 are NOT comparable: v3's prop_docs counted docblocks attached to no prop. Re-measure rather than trusting these.
caveat: Four propose-only Claude Code subagents work this backlog: ds-backlog-pilot (triage + dispatch), ds-metric-closer (DEV-1/DEV-2/GLOBAL-2), ds-gate-author (AGENT-3 + new metrics), ds-code-connect-mapper (AGENT-1). Each applies, measures, reverts, and leaves a patch in .agent-proposals/ for a human to git apply. None commits. GLOBAL-1, GLOBAL-3 and DEV-3 are fenced off from all of them by explicit human decision. agents/design-system-agent is unrelated: it turns one Figma node into a component and has never been run end-to-end.
verify: npm run ds:score --json | then read .parts[] for the named metric id

tasks.title: Make the expression scope reach the package
requirements: Fix the three typography holes first - 15 variables, 8 call sites - before betting 110 role variables on the same mechanism
Radix portals render to document.body and do not inherit the scope; re-apply it as notifications-drawer.tsx does
Give the core a neutral default: :root is currently the marketing expression, so unscoped surfaces are silently opted in
tasks.acceptance: ds:score expression_reach = 100, and --typo-h1-font-family resolves to the same face in the app and dist-pkg

tasks.title: Emit machine-readable component contracts
requirements: Add `features: { componentsManifest: true }` to .storybook/main.ts - it has no features block today
Record that the manifest schema is explicitly not stable and not a public API: consume, never fork
Confirm manifests/components.json actually contains props - a flag that emits an empty manifest is the failure mode this guards
tasks.acceptance: ds:score contracts_emitted = 100, and the built manifest has props for button and data-table

tasks.title: Give every gate a self-test
requirements: Extend the GATES table in scripts/check-gate-selftests.js
Each probe must make the gate exit non-zero AND name the probe - exiting non-zero alone is not evidence, since a crash looks identical
Write the probe inside the gate's own scan root, or it is never read and the gate passes for the wrong reason
Suspect the probe before the gate: the props probe first used size="default", which prop-compat.ts does not track
tasks.acceptance: check-gate-selftests.js exits 0 with 15 gates, and neutering any gate's failure branch takes it to exit 1 naming that gate

tasks.title: Raise Code Connect coverage
tasks.orchestrator_fit: closest of the nine to agents/design-system-agent's shape, via its code-connect-publisher subagent
requirements: Pick targets by Figma library-analytics usage, not alphabetically - Figma's eval ties the measured savings to coverage of real instances
Six legacy mappings point at deleted or deprecated MUI components: MegaMenu, Snackbar, SideNavigation, Radio, TextField, ChartMetricCard
Expect deletions, not only rewrites: ui/mega-menu is data-driven (items[]) against the legacy overlay's isOpen/onClose, so its example cannot be ported
Do NOT run figma:publish - it changes what every designer sees and runs from CI with a repository secret
tasks.acceptance: ds:score code_connect_coverage >= 51, and `npx figma connect parse --exit-on-unreadable-files` exits 0

tasks.title: Document props on the most-used components
requirements: A JSDoc block inside the exported *Props declaration is what makes Storybook Controls show a description
Prioritise by usage, not file order - avatar is 19 of 19 props undocumented
Document the three API traps: Button iconOnly silently discards children; Input has no adornment prop; Tooltip takes title, not content

A docblock must sit IMMEDIATELY BEFORE a prop line. An empty interface body containing only a comment does not count and never did -- react-docgen builds Controls descriptions per prop. v3's metric accepted it, which is how 14 hollow modules were produced; v4 does not.
tasks.history: 31 of 45 modules from the first ds-metric-closer patch applied in 4e1d87a (42 -> 65). The other 14 were hollow.

tasks.title: Forward refs from load-bearing modules
requirements: A React-19-only ref path is not enough - the peer range is ^18 || ^19
Prioritise form controls, overlays, and anything a consumer needs to focus or measure
forwardRef changes the public type surface: run build:package then pkg:types:check, because the published index.d.ts has shipped broken with all gates green

tasks.title: Convert directional spacing to logical properties
requirements: ms-/me-/ps-/pe- mirror with dir; ml-/mr-/pl-/pr- do not, so an RTL locale breaks the layout instead of flipping it
Mechanical but not blind: some are genuinely physical, such as an icon that must stay left regardless of direction. Leave those and comment why
Once the ratio is high, consider promoting composition:check's advisory to a failure for src/components/ui/ - the same ratchet used for hex
tasks.acceptance: ds:score rtl_readiness >= 80, and a story under dir="rtl" mirrors rather than breaking

tasks.title: Make user-facing strings translatable
tasks.size: S for the metric, L for the conversion
requirements: ADD THE METRIC FIRST - this is the one task with no ds:score entry, so there is nothing to verify against
Count only user-facing strings. A first pass counted displayName assignments like 'CardHeader' as copy; those are not user-visible and must not inflate the number
src/lib/format.ts already takes locale? and caches Intl formatters - reuse it rather than adding a second mechanism
Choose deliberately: a full i18n runtime is a large dependency for a component library. Strings as props with English defaults may be the right answer
tasks.acceptance: a new global-goal metric exists, is proven able to fall by mutation, and reports the real ratio

tasks.title: Type-check the test files
requirements: Add the test files to a tsconfig that `npx tsc -b` actually reaches, or give them their own project
Expect existing errors; fix them rather than loosening the config - a test asserting a dead signature is the defect this surfaces
Add a dev-goal metric so it cannot silently regress
tasks.acceptance: npx tsc -b covers all test files and exits 0, CONFIRMED with --listFiles rather than assumed - a run that silently excludes them also exits 0

tasks.title: Rework the 14 hollow prop docblocks
requirements: These 14 were left out of 4e1d87a because their docblock sat in an empty interface body, documenting nothing react-docgen can surface.
The prose is genuinely useful and should return ABOVE the declaration, where react-docgen reads it as the COMPONENT description rather than a prop description.
progress, select and slider were already hollow before any agent touched them -- pre-existing, not introduced.
A named exported Props type is still worth keeping even when every prop is inherited; the defect is where the comment sits, not that the interface exists.
tasks.acceptance: ds:score prop_docs >= 76, and no src/components/ui module has a Props interface whose only body content is a comment

tasks.title: Self-test the ds:score metrics, not just the gates
requirements: ADD THE METRIC FIRST if this is to be tracked -- it currently has none, like GLOBAL-3 and DEV-3.
Gates have check-gate-selftests.js; the 14 ds:score metrics have nothing equivalent, and prop_docs proved within hours of shipping that a metric can be satisfied without moving the thing it names.

A metric probe must assert BOTH directions: a change that should move it does, and a change that should NOT move it does not. prop_docs v4 was verified exactly this way -- a hollow docblock left the numerator at 49, a real one took it to 50.
Binary metrics are the priority: a typo in expression_reach or contracts_emitted reads as a permanent 0, indistinguishable from the real state.
tasks.acceptance: a harness exists that mutates each metric's input in both directions and fails if a metric does not discriminate

tasks.title: Material Symbols icon foundation + Toast/Alert to Figma V3

raw.detail: Toast/Alert do not match Figma V3 (full border not left bar, Elevation/Medium, optional icon/paragraph/timestamp); commit 7ee9dca shipped a wrong left-bar version. Icons to move to self-hosted Google Material Symbols (variable font).

requirements: Review approved in docs/tasks/toast-alert-icon-foundation.md BEFORE building. Open decisions there must be resolved first: fill strategy (A reuse / B new surface tokens / C color-mix; recommend B), info surface source, card radius 4 vs 8, Material Symbols style.

Icons: self-host material-symbols variable font (no CDN), <Icon> wrapper with FILL/weight axes (design uses FILL 1), Storybook Foundations/Icons page. Account for .size-limit.cjs. lucide stays for unmigrated components.
Border is a FULL 1px card border in status colour, NOT a left bar. status.{tone}.border already matches Figma exactly for all four statuses.
Toast elevation = shadow-xl (= Figma Elevation/Medium exact); Alert is flat. Icon, paragraph and timestamp are all OPTIONAL.
Do NOT repoint the shared status.{tone}.bg (Badge/Chip/StatCard depend on the near-white value); if B, add dedicated notification-surface tokens through the 3-tier pipeline, contrast-gated.
Supersede/revert the left-bar toast from commit 7ee9dca.
tasks.acceptance: Pixel diff of each coded status (Toast + Alert) against the Figma node reaches parity; governance:ci green; npm test green; size budget holds; dark-mode baseline unchanged or justified.
